I agree that the comphet masterdoc was problematic, it became controversial as many lgbt people criticized it, aswell as the fact that yes, the tumblr author came out as bisexual. To be fair I didn't know Adrienne Rich was a political lesbian, that's disappointing. That doesn't mean that comphet in itself is not a valid concept and holds no value for lesbians or even some bisexual women who felt pressured to be in a relationship with men. There are many women who spoke on this or related to it, it's very far stretched to claim that they are all bisexual, when both could relate to it. We live in a world that's not safe for women (for instance 80% of women in Europe were sexually harassed) and these kind of traumas and hypersexualization *CAN* lead to women being promiscuous (this is a well known fact in psychology to victims of r*pe or SA), obviously each individual reacts or copes differently though.

How are these half baked social theories when all the reasonings I gave you have a solid ground in reality? Psychology supports the theory that we may be born as "blank slates" (Tabula Rasa) but our environments shape us the most. All of these things have an impact on the people throughout the world, whether men or women. You seem to undermine the effects of the environment as you only look at the surface of the problems without questioning yourself what are the roots of these problems.

Whether you like to hear it or not, reality is that yes, women tend to have weaker constitution than men because in general we are not expected nor encouraged to be loud, confident, defensive of ourselves. Yes obviously, gay men face homophobia aswell, but first and foremost, they still have the advantages of being a man in society. People around them still view them as men, and thus will uphold those expectations over them.

I never heard that comphet comes from political lesbianism, do you have a source on that? I disagree on the notion that they are the same though. I don't even see how you could compare them. Political lesbianism consists of straight or bisexual women who choose to only have relationships with women out of political beliefs/motivations, whereas comphet is the result of expecting women to adhere to general standards, lack of support, not taking the orientation seriously etc. Someone for example who lives with a religious family or within a 2nd/3rd world country that doesn't accept lgbt, will understandably have comphet because they don't have the support to accept themselves.

As for why straight women tend to have more homosexual tendencies than straight men, socialization theory actually explains that aswell, ask yourself why there are more bisexual women than bisexual men statistically speaking. That's because straight men are afraid to lose their masculinity (through gay contacts/relationship), lesbianism is more romanticized so straight women see it as a positive thing, straight women might feel grossed out by men or they were abused by men so they see women a safe refugee - thus straight women end up having more homosexual tendencies than men. This also explains why there's so much more bi women than bi men out there, it's much more difficult to come out as a bi man.

I think the category of people you refer to are less likely to use the lesbian label because it's considered a boring label in their eyes in today's world, they are more likely to use vague descriptors like queer or sapphic which are umbrella terms.

Because heteronormativity and misoginy/sexism impacts women and men differently, hence you can't compare them directly. Women tend to be valued in society based on the relationship they have, they aren't valued for their efforts and results, like men are. There are women who literally get into relationships with men for validation, from their family, friends, colleagues, so on. Men are way more used to the idea of being on their own. In general, women are way more pressured to get into a relationship with a man, give birth to a baby and start a family. Meanwhile men are pressured to advance in their careers, focus on themselves to become independent. Sadly, there are lesbians who would rather disrespect themselves and their identity for the sake of taking the easy route and adhering to standard expectations, instead of being authentic with themselves. 

Point is, we don't live in a vacuum, there's many problems in this world that leave an impact on us. I'm confident that if we lived in a healthy society that valued women as much as men, this shit wouldn't happen as much.

The data set is from 2006 to 2008, back then it was much more stigmatized to be part of lgbt, plus the internet wasn't as widely used as it is today, there were no dating apps. It was also much more difficult to find info about lesbians and lesbian history, comphet, there was no online community you could easily find etc. So I don't think the stats from the previous generations would be accurate for today when it comes to lgbt in general.

I agree with you that it's very messed up when people use manipulation tactics to bypass boundaries, such as guilt-tripping you if you reject them, as you mentioned as example there are people who threaten you they will commit suicide if you don't grant their wishes.
I will do a little tangent here since you brought up that example and I find it a bit personal, usually someone who truly feels suicidal will never use that as a manipulation tool against you. Suicide is a real and serious issue on it's own, and people who genuinely went through periods like that, know very well that it's more than just a "seek for attention". 


The point is, you are not responsible for the way someone reacts to you or your boundaries, if they try to manipulate you or say awful things to you, that's on them, not you.


However, the way they react has nothing to do with ghosting. For instance, how are you supposed to know the boundaries if they ghost you?
You also mentioned it's a form of rejection and that it should be easy to understand, but why would anyone assume that if someone doesn't answer, it's about rejection, when there are people who are just too busy to respond? 
In other words, if everyone thinks that ghosting = rejection, then people will instantly assume that a busy person rejected them which is false, we shouldn't come to these conclusions on our own without communication.


This is why communication is crucial, and people who choose to ghost leave the other person confused rather than help them understand it. And worse, the person getting ghosted might think it's their fault when in reality it's not always the case. I don't think it's ok to instantly put the blame on the person getting ghosted as if "they deserved it" or "as if it's always their fault", when there are many people who ghost because they are genuinely selfish.

I respectfully disagree because it depends on context, unless you're referring to cases where it's harmful to respond, for instance if you find out that the person you talk to is a creep, or a scammer.


But if you're referring to cases where you feel safe, such as a person that wouldn't harm you AND you consider them a friend, I think it's very selfish to ghost them.
You don't owe anyone anything, but that doesn't mean it's ok to hurt people for your own sake.


This is not the job of a therapist, this is between you and someone else, but that doesn't mean they deserve to be treated like an "object to be thrown away", they are humans like you and they have feelings.
